lesson_title: Same R500, Three Prices: R1,60 vs R7 vs R70
hook_text: Withdrawing R500 can cost R1,60... or R70. Same money. Different door.
clip_script: Follow one R500 note out of the account by three different doors. Door one, the supermarket till: ask for cashback, pay R1,60. Door two, the bank's ATM: R2,00 plus R1,00 per hundred — R7,00, four times the till. Door three, the branch counter: R70,00 — enough to buy the bread forty times over. Now run the year. Weekly cash at the till: about R83 for the year. Weekly cash at the counter: R3 640. The difference could stock a spaza stall for a month. Same money, same year — the only variable was which door you made a habit of. Nobody loses their savings to one giant fee. They lose them R7 at a time, without watching.
visual_style: Three doors side by side with price tags; a R500 note walks through each, shedding coins — tiny at door one, a shower of notes at door three; year totals stack into two towers.
pacing: Three quick door reveals, then the slow shocking year comparison.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to pick the right account and dodge the fee traps.
